### Introduction

Energy management has established itself as a growing priority for organisations in all sectors and for public administrations. As the global energy landscape evolves, energy professionals face a number of challenges and opportunities that require adapting to new realities.

In its 8th edition, Spacewell Energy’s Energy Management Survey aims to capture a wide range of perspectives from energy experts, highlighting key trends, emerging priorities and common obstacles on the path to energy efficiency and sustainability goals.

This report presents the results of the survey, providing an overview of the goals shared by energy professionals, as well as the strategies and tools they use to address the most relevant challenges in their respective sectors. We have added some annotations and drawn conclusions based on the responses.

Highlights include the adoption of new technologies, the importance of energy costs and regulatory frameworks and resource optimisation, as well as the evolving role of energy management in corporate strategies.

We invite you to read the full analysis, where you will find valuable insights and useful information that can be key to guiding and improving your future energy management strategies.

And if you would like to go deeper into any of the topics or find out how Spacewell Energy can help you and your organisation with your energy efficiency strategies, please do not hesitate to contact us.

### Who has participated in the 2024 Energy Survey?

We start, as always, with the profile of the survey participants. 58% of the participants work in energy related companies, such as energy service companies (ESCOs), utilities or renewable specialists.

The remaining 42% work in non-energy organisations, including industry, hospitality or the public sector. In the report we refer to these companies as ‘end-customers’. These include Real Estate professionals and Facility Managers. However, in the graph they are shown in their own category, as sometimes they have a set of job descriptions that includes energy management, specially in the case of larga faciliti management teams.

Participants in the Energy Management Survey come from companies of widely varying sizes, ranging from self-employed and very small businesses, to organisations with more than 10,000 employees, as you can see on the graph.

For clarity, we have divided them in two groups:

` 65% are small and medium-sized enterprises, up to 200 employees. ` 35% are companies from 200 employees to more than 10,000 employees.

Within these companies, participants have both technical and management positions. They are mainly energy managers, commercial directors or CEOs, representing 70% of the total.

Other profiles include facility managers, sustainability managers and project managers.

The profile of End Customer companies is, as you might expect, heterogeneous. They are mainly companies from the industrial, real estate, hospitality and healthcare sectors. To a lesser extent, professionals from public administration, education and retail also participated.

From a geographical perspective, the main focus of respondents is Europe, with a majority from Spain and the UK, with contributions from Germany, Belgium and the Netherlands, and a small representation from Latin America.

Finally, there is also a great deal of variety in the number of buildings or establishments managed by each professional. From professionals who are not directly responsible for any building to some that exceed 100.

Why are we telling you all this? To give you an insight into the profile of the professionals who responded to the survey. So that you can understand the context of the information we are presenting and draw your own conclusions.

Now, let’s dive into the results.

### Managing Energy Costs

2024 has not been a year of rocketing energy costs as previous years were. However, managing these costs remains a priority in many organisations to gain operational efficiency and reduce overall spend.

70% of respondents perceived a slight increase in energy costs of around 5%, but there are hardly any cases of higher increases.

However, when viewed cumulatively, this 5% increase follows a substantial 20% rise reported in the 2022 survey, highlighting the growing financial burden. These compounding increases underscore the need for a more proactive approach to energy management, as even modest annual rises can add up to significant costs over time.

Even if this hasn’t been a year of large increases, cost savings are still the main reason why organisations in a variety of sectors seek the expertise of an energy services company. Even if they haven’t gone up, energy still represents a large percentage of overall costs. This is what professionals from energy services companies and end customers told us in this year’s survey.

Are we surprised by this response? Not really. Although sustainability and compliance are important reasons to implement energy saving measures (priority for 20%), it is the economic impact that is most tangible in an organisation. Numbers are clearly measurable and have an impact on the overall balance sheet.

##### Energy Savings Plans

70% of participants told us that their organisation has an energy efficiency plan. This figure is on a slight upward trend over the last few years. Back in 2016, 44% of participants said they had a strategy in place.

It is encouraging to see that many companies taking steps to become more energy efficient.

In the next edition of the survey we hope to include more information to understand what those plans are: awareness, energy conservation, use of energy monitoring technology, etc. Stay tuned.

##### Main Challenges in Managing Multiple Locations

48% of the respondents manage more than 10 buildings. Another 20% manage between 2 and 10... So we asked all of them, what are the biggest challenges in multi-location projects?

In order of importance, their responses are:

Getting budget for hardware installation 
Understanding which buildings to start in 
and prioritise 
Tracking expenses in a clear way 
Start with the first analysis 
Convincing decision-makers or management 
to do audits in some locations 

##### Hybrid Work and Energy Management

Since the outbreak of the pandemic, remote working and hybrid solutions have become standard throughout the world, especially in the services sector. Talk of hybrid or remote working is no longer new, but it is still an issue of interest in relation to energy efficiency.

It is also a social discussion that large companies are getting into about responsibility and what’s best for their business, but we won’t go that way for the purposes of this report.

Hybrid work environments drive organisations to optimise not only energy use but also workspace management, as both EMS and Integrated Workplace Management Solutions (IWMS) play a critical role in helping organisations achieve flexibility and efficiency without compromising operational effectiveness.

Respondents of the survey work in different combinations of remote, hybrid and in person:

To the 72% who offer hybrid working in some shape or form, we asked: does this affect the energy consumption and efficiency of your spaces?

49% indicate that they are more efficient now. These organisations have taken advantage of the new situation and have been able to manage varying occupancy levels and their energy use.

16% consider that they are less efficient, but are already working to address this. A small 3% consider that they are less efficient, and that they should implement strategies to address this. The remaining 30% did not want to make a choice

As you can see, almost 20% consider that they are less efficient with their current hybrid work setup. Is this your situation too? That brings the opportunity to look into new strategies to be more efficient in the workplace, with the help of an Energy Management System or even an Integrated Workplace Management System, depending on the specifics.

##### Energy Regulations: European Directives

Not so relevant if you work in the UK, but 2024 has been a busy year for energy efficiency regulation with the revision of the Energy Performance of Buildings Directive 2024/1275, shortly after the Energy Efficiency Directive 2023/1791.

We asked energy services companies whether customers have asked for information on these directives and how it affects them.

31% indicate that they have received enquiries from their customers about the Directives, both to find out about possible implications and to initiate energy efficiency projects. The remainder indicated that they had not received any related questions.

Do we expect changes in relation to this question? Yes, once the transposition has been made into local legislation and the Directives are clearly reflected in European countries’ regulations. Most likely by the end of 2025 and 2026. Are businesses prepared to act now to ensure compliance and seize opportunities ahead of their competitors?

### Focus: Energy Services Companies (ESCO)

We now focus on Energy Services Companies (ESCOs), their perspective and challenges in particular. These professionals, experts in energy management, have a very close relationship with end customers. They are the ones who are most exposed to the implementation of energy savings measures and their follow-up.

In the case of the participants in this survey, the ESCOs surveyed work with clients in sectors such as industry, public administration and real estate. From the initial project phase and the installation of hardware to the monitoring of energy consumption.

##### Top Challenges for Energy Professionals in 2024

Each organisation may have its own unique challenges depending on the type of company, business objectives, leadership, geography, and more... But there are a number of common elements that many professionals share.

To the question, what has been your main challenge this year?, the main answers, representing 80% of the votes, were:

Generating and maintaining verified savings 
Delivering the right energy saving measures to customers 
Improving operational efficiency 
Demonstrating the return on investment (ROI) on energy saving measures 
Identifying the technologies that fit their needs 

Being able to demonstrate the savings from energy efficiency measures is becoming more important every year.

Professionals not only want to implement energy efficiency measures, but also be able to monitor and demonstrate what has been achieved. Why? To ensure that the measures implemented are effective, and to sustain energy efficiency projects.

This point is closely linked to the need to evaluate the return on investment (ROI) and improve operational efficiency across the board.
